sections.heading: Need scalable capacity with stronger governance?
sections.body: Adding people alone does not establish a delivery capability. Organisations need defined ownership, engineering standards, quality controls and a sustainable way to retain knowledge. A Global Capability Centre (GCC) brings those elements into an operating model aligned to your business priorities.

sections.heading: Build capability you can govern and retain
sections.body: The intended outcome is a GCC with quality, security and engineering IP embedded, including a build-operate-transfer option. Define which capability, knowledge and operating responsibilities move to your organisation, and which software remains licensed. Measure readiness against agreed delivery standards, governance adoption and transfer acceptance criteria.

sections.heading: Buyer questions
sections.description: Clarify scope, evidence and accountability before agreeing an engagement.

items.title: How is a GCC different from adding specialists?
items.description: Staff augmentation adds specialists within your management structure. A GCC engagement also addresses the operating model, governance, tooling and knowledge retention; the build-operate-transfer option includes agreed handover obligations.

items.title: What transfers, and what remains licensed?
items.description: Define this in the IP register and contract. Knowledge, playbooks and agreed operating assets can be in the transfer scope; Linkfields proprietary software is not automatically transferred and may remain available by licence, subscription or SaaS.

items.title: Who manages work during build and operation?
items.description: The responsibility matrix defines the client sponsor, operational owners and Linkfields delivery responsibilities for each phase. Governance and decision rights change only through agreed phase acceptance.

items.title: How do you decide whether the centre is ready to transfer?
items.description: Agree acceptance criteria before the operating phase: knowledge handover, governance adoption, tooling access and delivery-control evidence. Transfer timing follows those criteria and contractual obligations, not an assumed setup duration.
